# The pure-Python packages a bundled entrypoint may import beside the standard
# library, and nothing else.
#
# Columns, tab-separated:  name <TAB> version <TAB> sha256 <TAB> reason
#
# Four rules, all of which build_packages.py enforces:
#
#   1. **Pure Python only.** A wheel with a compiled extension is a second ABI
#      to build for six platforms and a second thing a sandbox has to load. If
#      a package needs one, it is not an allowlist entry — it is a component.
#   2. **A pinned version and a digest.** The artifact is fetched by whoever
#      builds it and verified against this file, so "the latest" is never what
#      ships and a compromised index is a build failure rather than a release.
#   3. **A stated reason, naming the entrypoint that needs it.** A package
#      nothing imports is a package nobody has to audit and nobody removed.
#   4. **No transitive resolution.** Every package a build produces is a row
#      here, its dependencies included, because a dependency nobody wrote down
#      is a dependency nobody reviewed.
#
# The file is empty on purpose. No bundled entrypoint exists yet, so no package
# has an argued reason, and an allowlist seeded with plausible entries is an
# allowlist that was never reviewed. The first row arrives with the first
# entrypoint that needs it.
